name: Linux Fundamentals
description: Core Linux system administration skills including filesystem management, process control, user/permission management, package management, and service management.

subskills.name: File System Management
subskills.description: Understanding FHS, partitions, mounting, disk usage, and file system types (ext4, xfs, btrfs).

subskills.name: Process Management
subskills.description: Process lifecycle, signals, priorities, background/foreground tasks, and resource monitoring.

subskills.name: User & Permission Management
subskills.description: User/group management, file ownership, rwx permissions, SUID/SGID, sticky bit, sudo configuration.

subskills.name: Package Management
subskills.description: Installing, updating, removing packages using distribution-specific package managers.

subskills.name: Systemd & Service Management
subskills.description: Managing services, understanding unit files, boot process, targets, and journaling.

subskills.name: Shell & CLI Proficiency
subskills.description: Terminal navigation, piping, redirection, text processing, and environment variables.

subskills.name: File Operations & Text Processing
subskills.description: File manipulation, searching, sorting, and text stream processing.

subskills.name: Task Scheduling
subskills.description: Automating recurring tasks with cron jobs and at commands.

subskills.name: SSH & Remote Access
subskills.description: Secure remote access, key management, tunneling, and SCP/SFTP.

subskills.name: Advanced Storage & LVM Management
subskills.description: Logical Volume Management (pv/vg/lv), RAID concepts, swap management, and disk quotas.

github.signal: Linux-specific commands used in scripts (systemctl, apt, chmod, etc.)
SSH configuration files or key references
Linux-based Dockerfile (FROM ubuntu, alpine, debian, centos)

cv.signal: Specific Linux distribution mentioned (Ubuntu, CentOS, RHEL)

linkedin.signal: Linux or System Administration in job title/description

assessment.signal: Can navigate filesystem and use basic CLI commands
Can manage users, groups, and file permissions
Can configure and troubleshoot systemd services

junior.description: Can navigate the CLI, manage files and permissions, install packages, and monitor/manage processes.

mid.description: Can configure remote SSH access, automate tasks with cron, and handle filesystem mounting and disk inspections.

senior.description: Can author and harden systemd services, design LVM/RAID storage topologies, optimize kernel performance, and manage enterprise Linux servers.
